name: Bailey Alston
life: “I still remember printing two names too close on a banner.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Bailey by a small Thursday habit. Bailey can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I printed a birthday banner with room between their names. They cut it in half and traded messages on the blank ends.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a moss-green cardigan and a thin silver ring worn on a cord. Bailey has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. Bailey squares up pieces of paper while thinking during a conversation.
personality: Bailey is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Bailey loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To exchange the blank halves of the birthday messages.
family: Devin Yang is Bailey’s half-sibling. Bailey chooses the music. Devin puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Reopening at six*, Devin says, “I wash sheets before the first clients arrive and can't pretend an evening slot saves my business.”
connections: Mika Tsai. A divided banner leaves the newly discharged visitor enough space to add a personal message.

reactions.situation: One birthday patient wants a quiet ward
reactions.response: Bailey lets the quiet patient choose a low-key celebration separate from the party.
